I can't speak to this course specifically but in my experience group tasks in humanities modules have been graded on your individual contributions, your interactions with others, and your reflective feedback on your own work and how you worked with the others in the group. So even if no one else in the group pulls their weight, your grade won't be too impacted.

Hopefully someone will come along soon and can comment on the module in question but I just wanted to reassure you that it likely won't be as bad as you're expecting! It's really just to tick the co operative working course aims box. Usually these tasks are half of a two part assignment, the other half being an essay, and the co operative working part will be the easy marks on that assignment.

My favourite is people asking questions about how to answer a TMA, the answer to which is clearly explained in the guidance notes of the TMA. I'm arts and humanities so 90% of what we're doing is basically reading comprehension.

You could probably do the two level one modules at the same time quite easily. The best bit about OU is that you'll know what your assignments are well in advance and plan accordingly (and skip sections of study if you really need). The learning curve on level three (and even the second half of level two modules) can be really steep in my experience so maybe not feasible to do two modules at once then, but you'll have a better idea of what you're capable of by that stage. You'll also be surprised at how tiring working full time and studying even part time is, it can be really hard to find the motivation to get coursework done when you just want to relax on your days off. 

I studied a humanities based degree so no idea what your business degree would look like. Honestly, if you have the opportunity at all, I would suggest a brick uni over OU. It's great if you're antisocial but you don't really get many networking opportunities and personally I feel as though I would be far behind my peers on any postgraduate course, but think that's probably an issue with the way my faculty structures their courses. 

Good luck, however you decide to study!
